findings: IRQ14 interrupted ADD at 0x402012b0 and returned directly there. A then completed through SVC before B. IRQ17 interrupted the same ADD and returned to B entry. B SVC returned to the exact interrupted A PC; A then completed. Each epoch enters running A once.

The monitor enqueues saved A before releasing B at tick 1. Both have priority zero. Shared pop_ready ranks live job descriptors by period 2 vs 3 (RM) or relative deadline 2 vs 1 (DM). ELF dispatch scans candidates at 0x40201b28 onward, and validates and consumes the saved frame at 0x40201c20 onward; fresh A initialization at tick zero only.

Separate 16 KiB A/B/controller stacks start at 0x402040e0. Markers validate current stack top. A IRQ checks frame position below 16-byte local storage, x19=0xa19, stack sentinel and zero flag, valid SPSR, x20>0. IRQ sets flag and predicts x20+1 at captured ADD. Assembly validates restored sentinel, and continuation compares x20 to prediction. SVC checks worker frame position. Actual numeric x20 not exposed by -d int.

Worker calls trigger benchmark driver marker text. Driver validates id, epoch, tick, completion order, deadline, frame consumption and progress. UART alone does not independently identify scheduler choices. ELF exception-return targets and SVC boundaries corroborate both orders.

IRQ entry checks physical timer status and GIC interrupt ID, disables/masks timer and acknowledges GIC. IRQ18 checks empty jobs, consumed saved frame and 14 completions; emits terminal text and parks at 0x40201830 without rearm or eret. No events follow during quiet window.

limitations: One single-core Cortex-A72 QEMU TCG functional run. QEMU exception trace has PC and syndrome rather than register dumps; stack and live progress values are checked by the guest. No target hardware, latency bound or general schedulability measurements.
